bottleneck: Implanted electrodes trigger foreign-body responses: microglia and astrocytes encapsulate the device in glial scar, degrading signal quality over months to years. Stiff silicon shanks cause chronic mechanical injury with every brain micromotion, and the resulting inflammation further degrades the interface. The long-term effects of decades-long implants are simply unknown — no human has carried a high-channel cortical array for a full lifetime — so every chronic implant is an experiment in slow tissue rejection.
current_state: Flexible, tissue-soft electrodes reduce scarring in animals, but chronic human data beyond a few years is scarce. Biocompatibility for decades remains unproven and untestable on short timescales.

title: Electrode scarring degrades implants over years
why_it_blocks: A brain implant that the brain walls off is a temporary device, not a cure. Without lifetime biocompatibility, invasive BCIs cannot be offered to young patients who need them most and would carry them longest.
